title: Retry a failing Callable

blocks.text: The page's last interview answer re-submits a failed `Callable` up to a maximum number of retries, with **a new `Future` for each attempt**, and a timeout on each attempt. When every attempt has failed it throws the last failure, unwrapped from its `ExecutionException`, unless the cause is an `Error` (which is not an `Exception`): then the `ExecutionException` itself is thrown.

items: make at most `maxRetries + 1` attempts, each a fresh `submit(task)`, waiting at most 5 seconds for each;
an attempt that is still running after 5 seconds counts as failed (its failure is the `TimeoutException`), and is cancelled with an interrupt so it does not hold the executor's thread;
return the first attempt's result that succeeds;
if all fail, throw the **last** attempt's exception as described above.

blocks.text: Leave out the page's backoff sleep.

rows: hangs on the first attempt, then returns `"ok"` (single-thread executor); `1`

cases.says: A task that fails a few times and then succeeds gives its result, after exactly the attempts it needed.
A task that always fails is tried once plus maxRetries more times, and no more.
When every attempt fails, the last attempt's own exception is thrown, not the ExecutionException around it.
An attempt that does not finish within 5 seconds is cancelled, freeing the executor's thread, and the next attempt runs.
A task that throws an Error, which is not an Exception, ends in the ExecutionException that carries it.
When the last attempt times out, its TimeoutException is the failure thrown, not an earlier attempt's exception.
An attempt that takes 1 s succeeds on its own: each attempt gets the full 5 seconds.

concepts: A retry re-submits the Callable as a new Future for each attempt and, when all fail, throws the last cause.
